title: Bump an urgent job to the head of the queue
instruction: Move the red box onto the green pad, the first slot of the lane, and shift the other four boxes back one grey pad each, keeping their current order, so the lane holds the red box and then the other four in order on pads 2 to 5, with every box upright and centred within 2 cm of its pad's centre.
context: Compute clusters, batch schedulers and data pipelines run jobs from ordered queues, and an urgent job has to jump to the head while every waiting job keeps its place relative to the others. Doing this by hand is a sequencing problem: the lane has one free slot at the tail, so the jobs must be shifted back one at a time starting from the far end, or they collide. Automating queue handling and priority insertion is part of how AI labs keep scarce compute busy, so a robot that can reorder physical or digital queues without losing order touches the pace of AI work.
setup: Flat wooden table; all positions are in one fixed layout matching the screenshot. Two arm bases stand 30.5 cm either side of the midline (y = 0) on the base line (x = 0), facing +x. All distances below are in cm: x from the base line, y from the midline (L = left arm side, R = right arm side). Lane mat: one flat dark blue mat, 12 x 62 cm, 3 mm thick, centred at x 29.0, y 0. Five lane pads: flat square pads, 8 x 8 cm, 4 mm thick, centres at x 29.0 and y 24.0 L (pad 1, green, the head of the lane), 12.0 L (pad 2, grey), 0 (pad 3, grey), 12.0 R (pad 4, grey), 24.0 R (pad 5, grey). Intake mat: one flat dark blue mat, 10 x 10 cm, 3 mm thick, centred at x 41.0, y 24.0 L, with a yellow 8 x 8 cm pad (4 mm thick) on it. Boxes: five identical-size solid plastic boxes, 6 x 6 x 8 cm, 0.1 kg each, free to move, each centred on a pad: red on the yellow intake pad (x 41.0, y 24.0 L); blue on pad 1 (x 29.0, y 24.0 L); white on pad 2 (x 29.0, y 12.0 L); black on pad 3 (x 29.0, y 0); purple on pad 4 (x 29.0, y 12.0 R). Pad 5 is empty. Everything is fixed except the five boxes. Every box starts 12 cm or more from every other box, centre to centre.
scoring: All five boxes must be upright and resting on the table, or the score is 0. The red box centre must be within 2 cm of pad 1's centre, or 0. Each other box must be within 2 cm of the centre of one of pads 2 to 5, and those four boxes must fill pads 2 to 5 one each, or 0. Then: 1.0 if they are in their original order along the lane (blue on pad 2, white on pad 3, black on pad 4, purple on pad 5); 0.5 if exactly one neighbouring pair is swapped; 0 otherwise. A tape measure and a photo are enough.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put each box back on its starting pad, centre within 1 cm and upright, with its edges parallel to the pad edges.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid boxes and flat pads in simulation, friction 1.2 everywhere, boxes only turn about the vertical, no joints. The arms are weak and the 0.1 kg boxes are light. The pads are thin flat markers, not recesses, so a box can rest anywhere on them.
